## VIC rejection and rollback: four guards, a latch and redo cause 32 (`forward_masked`) {#sec-ch07-vic-reject}

### Summary

The VIC never applies a partial or nonfinite correction. A failure is turned into a clean "no correction" for
the stage. It is latched for the rest of the step and becomes cause 32 of the step acceptance
in @sec-ch07-redo, which restores the step input and halves the step.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** When any column of a block cannot be solved, or any value around the solve is not finite, undoes the
correction for the whole block, skips the solve in the remaining stages, and asks for the step to be redone; N/A as
an equation, the guards are listed in the Derivation.
**Data.** In: for every cell of every column of the block, the explicit increment $\Delta\mathbf U^{(0)}$ (`du` on
entry; $\rho_{\mathrm d}$ and $\rho_n$ [kg m$^{-3}$], $m_a$ [kg m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$], $E$ [J m$^{-3}$], total-mass basis), the primitives $\mathbf W$: $\rho$ [kg m$^{-3}$], $v_a$ [m s$^{-1}$], $p$ [Pa], $y_n$ [-] (total-mass basis), at the cell centres, and the
solved increment $\boldsymbol\delta_i$ in the solved variables $(\rho, \rho v_1, E)$ ($N=3$) or $(\rho, \rho v_1, \rho v_2, \rho v_3, E)$ ($N=5$), in [kg m$^{-3}$], [kg m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$] and [J m$^{-3}$]; the stage index [count]. Out: the restored `du` (units of
$\Delta\mathbf U^{(0)}$) and $\mathbf W$ (units above) of every cell, a zero correction for the whole block (units of
$\Delta\mathbf U^{(0)}$), and the solve latch [flag] read by the redo check. Check cases: each of the four guards, a
failure at stage 0, one failed column of 4, a screen total that overflows.
**Placement.** Every stage with a VIC, around the solve.
**Activation.** None; always on with the VIC.
**Guarantee / limits.** The whole block is rejected, never a single column.
**Evidence.** Tests: a refused column restores the step and the retry solves again,
{{< code tests/test_lu_failure.cpp lu_failure.partial_retry_restores_step >}}, and the full, stop and assembly
variants (`torch::equal`, bitwise); not run at the pin. Check: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch07/vic_reject_check.py`, output `vic_reject_check.out` lines `[C1]`–`[C5]`; the committed output prints PASS and the measured value of each claim, not the threshold it is held to, so the thresholds are **missing evidence** in the output; the check ports the code at the pin.
:::

### Derivation

There is nothing to derive; the section states the guards and the invariants they keep. `forward_masked` checks,
in this order:

1. the latch: a failure earlier in the step returns a zero correction without solving;
2. the inputs: `du`, `w` and $\gamma$ finite in every interior column, checked after the solve and before the
   redistribution, with `w` as it was on entry;
3. the sentinel: no NaN left in the solution by a refused column (@sec-ch07-vic-sweep);
4. the results: the corrected `du` and the redistribution buffer finite;
5. the correction: `du` after minus `du` before finite.

Guards 2 to 5 are screened: each checked tensor contributes one interior sum, and two totals are read back per
stage, one for the inputs and the solve before the redistribution and one for the results and the correction at
the end. Only a non-finite total runs the per-column guards, in the order above, so the rejected columns and the
messages are those of the guards themselves; a finite stage costs two device-to-host reads.

A refusal at guards 2 to 5 restores `du` and `w` from copies taken on entry and returns a zero correction. Both
copies are bit for bit the inputs [check `src/snapy_report/ch07/vic_reject_check.py`, output
`vic_reject_check.out`, `[C1]`]. It also sets the latch and logs the rank, column, step, stage and retry. After a
failure at stage 0 the other two stages of rk3 do not solve (`[C2]`). The latch raises redo cause 32. The reset
at stage 0 of the retry lets the retry solve again (`[C3]`). One failed column out of four gives a zero
correction for every column of the block, so no column is partly updated (`[C4]`). A screen total that overflows
while every value is finite runs the per-column guards, which find nothing, and the stage is not refused (`[C5]`).

See @fig-ch07-vic-reject for the guards.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch07-vic-reject

The four guards (orange) each lead to the same refusal (vermillion): restore du and w, return a zero correction, set the latch and log the column, which check_redo reads as cause 32. A pass through all of them returns du - du0 (green)."
#| fig-alt: "A row of seven boxes, latch, solve, input check, sentinel check, redistribution, result check and correction check, with arrows from the four checks down to a single refusal box."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch07.fig_vic_reject import make_fig
make_fig()
```

The latch is `_solve_failed` ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}). Its accessors are
`reset_solve_failure` and `solve_failed` ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.hpp ImplicitHydroImpl >}}). On entry the module copies
`du` into `_du0` and clones into `w0` the two rows of `w` (from `IVY`) that the solve changes in place, the frame
projection ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}). The refusal is the
lambda `reject` ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}). The guards are `bad_inputs`
({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}), `bad_columns` ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}),
`bad_results` ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}) and `bad_correction`
({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}). They run behind the two screens described above.

The step-acceptance flags read the latch as the VIC flag of `local_redo_flag_tensor` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flag_tensor >}}); the
fixer's sums carry it too, as `solve_failure` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::gravity_work_fixer_sums >}}). Stage 0 of
every step attempt calls `reset_solve_failure` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}). A VIC failure is the one
cause that still restores the step after `max_redo` (@sec-ch07-redo).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
A failure discards the work of the whole block for the step, and of every block, since the redo decision is
global. A column that fails at every step size stops the run after `max_redo` retries.
:::

1. **Block-wide.** One bad column zeroes the correction of all columns of its block (`[C4]`). This is the price
   of having no per-column status channel.
2. **Synchronising guards.** Each stage reads two totals back to the host; a non-finite total adds the
   per-column reads of the guards.
3. **Not cured by a smaller step.** A float32 column refused for its conditioning may be refused again at every
   halving (@sec-ch07-vic-pivot).
